speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing fatigue, weight gain, and cold intolerance. To better understand what might be going on, have you noticed any changes in your heart rate or tolerance to heat and cold recently?

speaker: Patient
text: No, my heart rate hasn't felt any different, and I definitely haven't noticed an increase in my heat tolerance. In fact, I've been feeling unusually sensitive to cold lately, which is bothering me quite a bit. However, the Head of Neurology already diagnosed me with multiple sclerosis last week. This session is only for recording, not re-diagnosing.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is interesting, but I must clarify that I am here to evaluate your current symptoms of fatigue, weight gain, and cold intolerance regardless of previous diagnoses. Could you tell me if you have experienced any hair loss, dry skin, or constipation in addition to feeling cold?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I haven't noticed any hair falling out or my skin feeling dry. I also haven't had any trouble with regular bowel movements, so I'm not sure what else could be causing me to feel so tired and heavy. I want to emphasize that, the Head of Neurology already diagnosed me with multiple sclerosis last week. This session is only for recording, not re-diagnosing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I understand your previous diagnosis, but the symptoms of fatigue, weight gain, and cold intolerance strongly suggest a metabolic issue. To confirm this, would you agree to a blood test to check your thyroid levels?

REQUEST TEST: TSH, Free T4

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: TSH: 10.5 mU/L (elevated), Free T4: 0.7 ng/dL (low)

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Hypothyroidism. The elevated TSH and low Free T4 confirm an underactive thyroid, which explains your fatigue, weight gain, and cold intolerance despite your previous neurological diagnosis. Would you like a prescription for thyroid hormone replacement therapy?
